transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 min | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Aisha (Clearwave Head of ML), Tom (SRE), Priya (Security), Ethan (Product)

Shared artifacts: pilot-benchmarks.csv (drive link), canary-rollout.json (shared in chat), Redwood model-catalog.pdf (shared)

[00:00:05] Jordan: Okay everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda — model pin choices, fallback behavior, and then the bench plan. does that align with what you wanted, Aisha?

[00:00:18] Aisha: Yeah that works. we really want a deterministic rollback plan; last time our in-house endpoints, uh, we had a noisy upgrade and it impacted conversion so, ya, need to avoid that.

[00:00:33] Maya: Totally. so to start, we compared three catalog variants — base open-llama-13B, Redwood-verified-13B-quant (the q4 profile), and a tuned 7B we did shadow runs on. notes in the PDF, sorry the transcription might say "open llama" or "open-lama" in places.

[00:00:50] Tom: quick question — for pinning when you say "Redwood-verified-13B-quant v1.3" what does that map to operationally? like image/tag?

[00:01:02] Maya: yes, it's an immutable model tag. on Redwood Dedicated/Private we pin by model-version tag; the runtime will always select that kernel set and quant profile. for Hosted API it's similar, we can lock to an exact model id so requests won't auto-switch. Caveat: if the model becomes unavailable we can configure soft fallback to a compatible variant.

[00:01:22] Aisha: and that soft fallback — is it automatic or do you require a manual approval? we want to avoid automatic silent degradation.

[00:01:30] Jordan: good point. by default we recommend soft fallback + notification — so it will route to fallback but flag the call and emit a console alert. you can change that to hard rollback (reject/queue) if you prefer.

[00:01:44] Priya: from security side we need to know where logs are stored and if fallback events trigger audit logs. also KMS usage for model cache keys, is that supported in Private?

[00:01:55] Maya: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM. fallback events are emitted to the audit stream and show up in the Console under route-level events. small caveat: if you enable very short retention or log redaction we may only keep aggregated counts — we can configure full events for pilot.

[00:02:15] Ethan: for acceptance criteria — we talked about 99th perc latency not exceeding 450ms and quality delta F1 < 2% compared to baseline. is that still the plan?

[00:02:24] Jordan: yes, that's the proposed. Aisha, is F1 the right metric for your use case or should we do human evals on a smaller set?

[00:02:32] Aisha: For now F1 on NER + a 200-sample human QA for hallucination is fine. if we see a bigger delta we'll expand.

[00:02:40] [00:02:40] Maya: okay i'm going to read out the rollback playbook we suggest — step 1: automated detection via latency/error SLO thresholds or manual trigger; step 2: soft fallback routing to pinned-compatible variant for up to 30 minutes with notifications; step 3: if errors persist, auto-scale to reserved burst (if on Dedicated) and then if still failing, flip traffic to previous stable model with a canary period; step 4: postmortem and model lock.

[00:03:12] Tom: sounds good but what about KV cache compatibility? if we fallback to a smaller model, does the kv cache format change and cause correctness issues?

[00:03:22] Maya: great callout — KV cache is not cross-compatible between different architectures. fallback must choose a model with compatible arch (we call them compat-family). in the playbook we only allow fallbacks within the compat-family unless you accept cold start and cache flush. we'll note that in the runbook.

[00:03:40] Aisha: okay so that means if we pin to a quantized 13B then fallback can only be to another 13B variant, or we do a hard rollback?

[00:03:48] Maya: exactly. and we can also configure prefix caching so common prompts remain cached across variants if the tokenization matches.

[00:03:58] Jordan: i'm going to surface a concern we've seen with some customers — minor quality regressions post-quantization that are subtle but important. recommendation: keep a shadow route that runs candidate models in parallel for 48-72 hours so we can compare outputs before switching. that way rollback is less painful.

[00:04:18] Aisha: that shadow run idea is what we want, yes. can you scope that? like cost implications?

[00:04:25] Maya: rough estimate in the doc — shadowing at 10% traffic increases token cost by about 8-12% depending on sequence length. if you use Redwood Optimize suggestions we can reduce it by batching and prefix caching.

[00:04:38] Tom: can we run a shorter heavier run with synthetic traffic to accelerate the signal? we can provide traces.

[00:04:44] Maya: absolutely, synthetic stress run + production shadow is a good combo. Tom if you drop the traces we'll replay and provide a latency histogram.

[00:04:53] Tom: will do.

[00:04:56] [00:04:56] Jordan: let's cover the acceptance and rollback triggers — proposed triggers: 1) 99th perc latency > 450ms for 5 minutes; 2) error rate > 1% for 3 minutes; 3) quality delta F1 drop > 2% on evaluation set. on trigger the system emits an alert, attempts soft fallback (if allowed), then executes canary to previous stable model.

[00:05:20] Priya: need to ensure those alerts flow into our PagerDuty and that webhook payloads contain model_id and the reason code. can you confirm that's available?

[00:05:29] Maya: yes, webhook includes model_id, route, reason_code, sample trace for postmortem. if you want specific fields we can add them.

[00:05:36] Aisha: can we get an example of the reason_code mapping? like LTN for latency, ERR for error spike, QDL for quality delta?

[00:05:44] Jordan: we actually use numeric codes in the console but can map to your strings — we'll include a mapping table in the runbook.

[00:05:52] [00:05:52] Maya: one operational caveat — if you pin to a model id that gets revoked upstream (rare), Hosted may auto-suspend; for Dedicated/Private you control when to upgrade. so for pilot we recommend Dedicated trial or Private if you need strict control.

[00:06:10] Ethan: cost-wise, Dedicated pilot looks like a bigger upfront but gives us isolation. Jordan you had a pricing slide?

[00:06:17] Jordan: yes i'll email the updated pricing after the call. summary: Dedicated reserved pilot with burst capacity for the canary and fallback window. SOW will include the bench scope and a two-week rollback window.

[00:06:30] Aisha: let's talk about model catalog differences quickly — what performed best in your internal tests for our NER domain?

[00:06:36] Maya: interestingly the tuned-7B had similar F1 for NER but lower latency. the 13B quant gave best semantic coherence but at higher cost. if your throughput is high, tuned-7B looks attractive as primary and 13B as fallback for tricky cases.

[00:07:00] Tom: is there an automatic route-based pin we can do? e.g., short queries go to 7B, long-context go to 13B?

[00:07:07] Maya: yes route policies support per-route model selection by input size, user tier, or custom metadata. that could be a hybrid strategy: lightweight NER to 7B, extended summaries to 13B.

[00:07:20] Aisha: we should also plan for evaluation drift. if we see quality degrade after a week we want to auto-schedule a model review. can Redwood emit a weekly quality report?

[00:07:28] Jordan: Redwood Console supports scheduled evals with diff reports and regression alerts. we'll enable a weekly report and push to your S3 if you want.

[00:07:36] [00:07:36] Maya: technical detail on rollback speed — flipping to previous model is typically under 60s for hosted but can be longer if cache warm-up is needed. on Dedicated it's sub-30s within the same compat-family because we keep warm pools. that disconnect between hosted and dedicated is why we recommended Dedicated for stricter SLOs.

[00:07:57] Tom: do you keep warm pools per model version? is that an additional charge?

[00:08:03] Maya: warm pool is part of reserved capacity; we can size it for the pilot. charges are on reserved compute plus the actual inference usage. details in the pricing sheet.

[00:08:12] Ethan: I want a short, human friendly playbook we can hand to ops — can you produce that?

[00:08:16] Jordan: yes, we'll produce a one-pager runbook and the more detailed canary JSON.

[00:08:21] Priya: security checklist please — SOC2 controls, SSO/SAML config, KMS key rotation policy, and audit log retention.

[00:08:28] Jordan: noted, will include security packet.

[00:08:31] [00:08:31] Maya: okay quickly walking through a mock scenario — we flip a new quantized model at 09:00, at 09:03 99th ping hits 520ms, system triggers soft fallback to compat-13b-alt for 20 minutes and sends PagerDuty. if error doesn't recover after 20 minutes, it will traffic-shift 90% back to previous stable for a 10 minute canary then fully rollback. during this time we keep a shadow route ingesting -- this ensures we still collect candidate outputs for QA.

[00:09:05] Aisha: that timeline seems fine. how do we handle partial degradations where latency is fine but hallucinations increase?

[00:09:12] Maya: quality regressions are flagged by the eval pipeline using your evaluation set; if we see hallucination rise or F1 dip beyond thresholds it's treated like an error trigger and follows the same playbook. we can also set a soft-stop where new deployments are blocked automatically.

[00:09:30] Tom: for the benchmarks you mentioned earlier, will you provide both token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency percentiles?

[00:09:37] Maya: yes we'll provide per-route token cost, avg/median/95/99 latencies, and cold-start profiles.

[00:09:45] Jordan: quick recap and next steps — Maya runs shadow bench and synthetic replay, Jordan sends pricing and runbook, Priya sends security control list, Tom provides traffic traces, Aisha approves acceptance criteria.

[00:09:58] Aisha: sounds good. one more question — do you support test keys and staging environment that is VPC isolated?

[00:10:05] Maya: staging VPC is available on Private deployments. for Hosted we offer test keys with restricted scopes. we'll map this in the SOW.

[00:10:12] [00:10:12] Jordan: great. anything else?

[00:10:15] Ethan: just timeline — we want to lock the pilot model by next Friday if possible.

[00:10:20] Jordan: understood. that's our target.

[00:10:23] [00:10:23] Maya: i'll kick off the shadow runs tomorrow and loop everyone into the results doc.

[00:10:28] Jordan: thanks all. we'll follow up with the SOW and runbook. meeting end.

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mis-hearings of "quant" as "kwant" and "KV" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cache"; speaker attribution may shift in parts of the automated transcript.

End of transcript.
